_meanings:
.²1 Knowledge, wisdom, intelligence, understanding; {#yajjIvyate kzaRamapi#}
 {#praTitaM manuzyErvijYAnaSOryaviBavAryaguREH sametam . tannAma jIvitamiha …#}
 <ls>Pt. 1. 24</ls>, <ls n="Pt.">5. 3</ls>; {#vijYAnamayaH koSaH#} ‘the sheath of intelligence’
 (the first of the five sheaths of the soul).
.²2 Discrimination, discernment.
.²3 Skill, proficiency; {#prayogavijYAnam#} <ls>Ś. 1. 2</ls>.
.²4 Worldly or profane knowledge, knowledge derived from worldly experience
 (<ab>opp.</ab> {#jYAna#} which is ‘knowledge of Brahma or Supreme Spirit’); {#jYAnaM#}
 {#te'haM savijYAnamidaM vakzyAmyaSezataH#} <ls>Bg. 7. 2</ls>, <ls n="Bg.">3. 41</ls>, <ls n="Bg.">6. 8</ls>; (the whole
 of the 7th Adhyāya of <ls>Bg.</ls> explains {#jYAna#} and {#vijYAna#}).
.²5 Business, employment.
.²6 Music.
.²7 Knowledge of the fourteen lores.
.²8 The organ of knowledge; {#paYcavijYAnacetane#} ({#SarIre#}) <ls>Mb. 12. 187. 12</ls>.
.²9 Knowledge beyond the cognisance of the senses ({#atIndriyavizaya#});
 {#vijYAnaM hi mahadBrazwam#} <ls>Rām. 3. 71. 30</ls>.
.²10 Information; {#labDavijYAnam#} <ls>Mb. 12. 44. 5</ls>.

<ab>N.</ab> of the author of the Mitākṣarā, a commentary on
 Yājñavalkyaʼs Smṛti.

means of arriving at correct knowledge ({#pramARa#}); {#kena#}
 {#vijYAnayogena matiScittaM samAsTitA#} <ls>Mb. 14. 21. 11</ls>.
the theory of knowledge, the doctrine taught by Buddha.

one of the five {#skanDa#}s postulated in the Buddhistic
 philosophy ({#rUpavedanAvijYAnasaMjYAsaMskArAH kzaRikavijYAnaskanDe smftiranupapannA#})
 <ls>ŚB. on MS. 1. 1. 5</ls>.
